title: How Noah's Ark Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the story of Noah's Ark and the Great Flood. They compare flood legends across cultures (Sumerian Ziusudra, the Epic of Gilgamesh and its Utnapishtim, the Bible, and the Quran), discuss why a worldwide flood is physically implausible and how a regional flood could have inspired the story, and examine the Black Sea deluge hypothesis (Ryan and Pitman, Ballard's expedition). They cover the cubit and the boat's size, the search for the ark on Mount Ararat and Mount Suleiman, the 1990s CBS "Incredible Discovery of Noah's Ark" hoax hosted by Darren McGavin, and the Ararat anomaly photos. The episode closes with live show and TV pilot announcements and listener mail from Sarah.
topics: Ryan and Pitman Black Sea flood
Incredible Discovery of Noah's Ark CBS hoax

segments.title: Opening banter and Zeitgeist
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with sponsor-style banter and talk about the movie Zeitgeist and its claims that religious figures trace back to ancient Egyptian gods, which leads to the question of whether similar flood stories show a real event or cultural borrowing.

segments.title: The Noah story and a global flood
segments.summary: They outline the flood legend: a man warned by God builds a boat and takes pairs of animals, and is mocked by neighbors. They note the moral lesson and argue that a literal worldwide flood covering the mountaintops is physically impossible, so the 'world' may have meant the known regional world. They also briefly discuss Bible literalists.

segments.title: Black Sea deluge hypothesis
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Noah's Flood hypothesis, also called the Black Sea deluge theory. Ryan and Pittman proposed rising Mediterranean waters poured into the Black Sea after the last ice age. Ballard's work suggested the Black Sea was once a freshwater lake. Later studies (2007 Greenland meltwater; a 2009 UNESCO and IUGS study) suggested a slower, milder rise over centuries to a millennium.

segments.title: Rain duration, regional floods, and the Mesopotamian origins
segments.summary: They discuss the biblical rainfall duration (forty days and nights, with reference to 150 days of waters) and the seven pairs of clean animals. They describe seasonal flooding of the Tigris and Euphrates and propose that Mesopotamian floods inspired the story. They trace the Sumerian Ziusudra, the Epic of Gilgamesh and its Utnapishtim, and the boat size shared across traditions.

segments.title: Cubits and the ark's size
segments.summary: The hosts explain the cubit as an ancient length measure, from the middle fingertip to the inside of the elbow, roughly 18 inches or 45.72 centimeters. They convert the Bible's 300 cubit length to about 450 feet, and say the ark would cover about an acre. They note the specific dimensions recur across traditions and question whether it was literal or hyperbolic.

segments.title: Noah in Islam and the Quran
segments.summary: The hosts describe Noah in the Quran as one of the five prophets of Islam, with Abraham, Jesus, Moses and Adam. The Quran's account of Noah is similar but differs in names and where the ark lands, Mount Judi rather than Mount Ararat.

segments.title: Search for the ark and the Incredible Discovery hoax
segments.summary: They discuss searches for the ark on Mount Ararat, the Mount Suleiman site in Iran, and the Ararat anomaly photos from CIA imagery. They describe the 1990s CBS special 'The Incredible Discovery of Noah's Ark', hosted by Darren McGavin, whose claims came from George Jamal, an actor who invented a companion named Vladimir and a story of finding the ark.

segments.title: Ballard's approach and Mount Suleiman rock formation
segments.summary: Robert Ballard's Black Sea expedition sought evidence of a flood rather than the ark itself; they found ancient freshwater shorelines and mussels, and ancient wood, but no Neolithic structures. Mount Suleiman's shape resembles a boat, but it is petrified wood or rock, and Answers in Genesis agreed it looked like rock.

segments.title: Live show and TV pilot announcement
segments.summary: Announcement of South by Southwest live podcast and a live variety show in Austin, plus the Science Channel TV pilot debut.

segments.title: Listener mail from Sarah
segments.summary: Sarah, a fourteen-year-old listener, writes about starting high school and her many activities, and suggests topics such as macaroni phobia and public television. The hosts ask for listener suggestions about biblical locations and Austin restaurants.
